metadata.title: Ford–Fulkerson: The Edge That Undoes a Mistake

beats.new_visual_element: ROLE HOOK · BrutalistHesitantWriter; silent mystery question, zero static card.

props.text:
A legal path sends flow.
So why can it trap us
one unit too soon?

beats.narration_text: This network can carry two units from s to t. But choose s–a–b–t first, and its bottleneck sends one. Every visible forward route now looks blocked.
beats.tts_normalized_text: This network can carry two units from s to t. But choose s a b t first, and its bottleneck sends one. Every visible forward route now looks blocked.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 1 · Bad middle augmenting path runs completely on split stage.

beats.narration_text: Reset. Send one along s–a–t, then one along s–b–t. The same capacities deliver two. So legal augmenting paths are not equally helpful in the moment.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Reset. Send one along s a t, then one along s b t. The same capacities deliver two. So legal augmenting paths are not equally helpful in the moment.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 2 · Two outer paths run fully; total reaches two.

beats.narration_text: Return to the bad first path. Before we quit at flow one, predict what edge the residual graph must add if the earlier choice is allowed to change.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Return to the bad first path. Before we quit at flow one, predict what edge the residual graph must add if the earlier choice is allowed to change.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PREDICT · Bad state holds; question writes on with highlighter wash.

beats.narration_text: The used edge a–b creates a backward residual edge b–a with capacity one. That edge does not send negative cargo; it cancels one unit of an earlier commitment.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The used edge a b creates a backward residual edge b a with capacity one. That edge does not send negative cargo; it cancels one unit of an earlier commitment.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE TRACE 1 / TRANSFORM · Reverse residual edge emerges from used middle edge.

beats.narration_text: Now the residual path s–b–a–t uses that backward edge. Augmenting once removes flow from a–b and reroutes it onto the two outer paths. Total flow becomes two.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Now the residual path s b a t uses that backward edge. Augmenting once removes flow from a b and reroutes it onto the two outer paths. Total flow becomes two.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE TRACE 2 / TRANSFORM · Repair path cancels middle flow and reroutes to outer edges.

beats.narration_text: The license is reversibility through residual edges. Forward capacity records what we may still add; backward capacity records what we may undo. Integrality makes each augmentation visible in whole units here.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The license is reversibility through residual edges. Forward capacity records what we may still add; backward capacity records what we may undo. Integrality makes each augmentation visible in whole units here.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE ABSTRACTION · Characteristics reversibility and integrality named after two instances and traces.

beats.narration_text: Each augmentation preserves capacity limits and flow conservation. If no residual s-to-t path remains, the vertices still reachable from s define a cut with every crossing edge full, so the flow equals that cut’s capacity and cannot be improved.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Each augmentation preserves capacity limits and flow conservation. If no residual s to t path remains, the vertices still reachable from s define a cut with every crossing edge full, so the flow equals that cut's capacity and cannot be improved.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PROOF · Reachable set and saturated cut animate on live final graph.

beats.narration_text: Back at the opening trap, greedy path choice was never promised to be locally wise. Ford–Fulkerson survives because residual edges can repair it before the no-path stopping test.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Back at the opening trap, greedy path choice was never promised to be locally wise. Ford Fulkerson survives because residual edges can repair it before the no path stopping test.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PAYOFF · Same hook network returns; bad path transforms into repaired flow.

beats.narration_text: The verdict: an augmenting path is a reversible commitment. Forward edges add room; backward edges return room. Stop only when the residual graph has no source-to-sink path.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The verdict: an augmenting path is a reversible commitment. Forward edges add room; backward edges return room. Stop only when the residual graph has no source to sink path.

artifactLines: A legal path can be locally unhelpful
Backward residual edges cancel earlier flow
No residual s→t path certifies the maximum

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Trace the bad path, construct every residual edge, then find the repair path and explain why the final no-path condition certifies maximum flow.

output: Track flow / capacity on every edge

beats.narration_text: Ford–Fulkerson is not safe because every path is smart; it is safe because residual paths can undo mistakes. Thanks for watching.
